data.summary: The "c23" directory defines a single AIO scenario that provisions a C23 development environment: a clang-22 toolchain from apt.llvm.org plus reused gcc-12 and supporting C tools (gdb/cmake/ninja/valgrind/cppcheck/strace). It is a declarative config/infrastructure layer consisting of a scenario metadata file (scenario.toml) consumed by `aio-config gen` and the Dockerfile fragment that performs the actual installation. No application business logic lives here; its value is in reproducible environment provisioning.

file_insights.name: scenario.toml
file_insights.summary: Scenario metadata describing the "c23" C23 development environment entry, consumed by the `aio-config gen` fragment-resolution tool.
file_insights.source_summary: A short TOML document with five top-level keys: id = "c23", name = "C23 开发环境", description (clang-22 full C23 toolchain via apt.llvm.org plus gcc-12 reuse and C tooling installed to system paths), category = "lang", and installer = "apt". Comments explain that the fragment.Dockerfile next to it holds the install steps.
file_insights.detailed_description: This file is the registry/manifest entry for the c23 scenario; the generator reads it to discover and resolve the adjacent Dockerfile fragment. It declares identity (id, name), a human-readable description, a category of "lang", and the installer type "apt". Without it the fragment would not be discoverable or selectable by the build tooling.
responsibilities: Declare the unique scenario id and display name
Expose a human-readable description of the environment
Classify the scenario (category=lang) and installer (apt) for the generator
Point the generator at the sibling fragment.Dockerfile for resolution

file_insights.name: fragment.Dockerfile
file_insights.summary: Dockerfile fragment that installs the clang-22 full C23 toolchain (apt.llvm.org bookworm repo), reuses gcc-12 from build-essential, and adds C companion tools to system paths.
file_insights.source_summary: A shell/Dockerfile instruction fragment (truncated in the provided excerpt) consisting mainly of explanatory comments plus apt repository setup and package install steps: adding the apt.llvm.org bookworm source and keys, installing clang-22/clang++/clang-format/clang-tidy/clangd and C tooling such as gdb, cmake, ninja, valgrind, cppcheck and strace, while relying on the head image's build-essential for gcc-12 instead of reinstalling it.
file_insights.detailed_description: This is the executable payload of the c23 scenario: a build fragment concatenated into a larger generated image definition. Its comments explain the design constraint that bookworm apt only ships gcc-12 (partial C23, -std=c2x) and that pulling newer gcc from other suites would upgrade libc6 and break the image, so full C23 support is delegated to clang-22 from the official apt.llvm.org bookworm repository (which requires libc6 >= 2.34, satisfied by bookworm's 2.36). All binaries are installed to system paths (/usr/bin, /usr/local/bin) so they are not shadowed by the shared aio_workspace volume, and it provides unsuffixed commands (clang, clang++, clang-format, clang-tidy, clangd, ...).
responsibilities: Add the official apt.llvm.org bookworm repository and signing keys
Install clang-22 and the full C23 toolchain plus clang-format/clang-tidy/clangd
Install companion C tooling (gdb, cmake, ninja, valgrind, cppcheck, strace)
Reuse gcc-12 from the base image's build-essential rather than reinstalling
Place all tools on system paths and expose versionless command names
